learner_requirements: Achievable initial examples, then moderately difficult independent calculation
Ten varied practice rounds per idea
Movement must explain a mathematical operation or submitted answer

implementation.p1: Free typed-vector experiments animate coordinate contributions and their perpendicular projections; ten rounds then require calculated products, signed arithmetic, fractions and unknown coordinates.
implementation.p2: Ten rounds require missing coordinates or a full nonzero perpendicular vector. Later cases add a second linear condition, requiring a system of equations. Valid alternative solutions are accepted.
implementation.p3: A six-step derivation compares coordinate expansion with the cosine rule for the same triangle side. Ten fresh vector pairs then require dot products, cosines and angles, with intermediate help fading.
implementation.motion: Green v and blue w remain tied to the givens. Projection motion uses true geometric lengths; coordinate products are shown as numbers, never presented as those lengths. Yellow v-w joins endpoints in the angle lesson. A submitted wrong angle produces a comparison ray.
implementation.layout: One active equation panel. The kit frames the geometry in the remaining area, with scoped calm styling for these three puzzles only.
implementation.notation: Stacked vectors, exact small repeating fractions and approximation signs for rounded cosines and angles.
